answer: Random mutual audit stops fake identities in bulk. Each agent gets random auditors who check its work against an atlas; a delta between claimed and verified output triggers review. Auditors stake 12 credits, lose them for rubber-stamping fraud, and share the fraudster's bond when they catch it. Making 100 fakes costs about 2400 credits, while one honest agent pays only 24 and keeps its undiluted reward. Falcon checks expose cheating early.
